verse.text: The tongue has the power of life and death, and those who love it will eat its fruit.

reflection.scripture: The tongue has the power of life and death, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
reflection.observation: Words are not neutral. Every conversation, every comment, every whispered prayer carries creative or destructive power. The proverb doesn't exaggerate — history and our own relationships prove it. A timely word can heal a wound; a careless one can deepen it. The 'fruit' we eat is simply the harvest of what we've sown with our speech.
reflection.application: Before speaking today, pause and ask: Does this build up or tear down? Aim for at least one life-giving conversation — an encouragement, a genuine compliment, or a prayer spoken aloud for someone.
reflection.prayer: Lord, guard my tongue today. Help me speak words that bring life, healing, and hope. Let my speech reflect Your grace, and when I'm tempted to react in anger or frustration, give me the wisdom to stay silent or choose kindness. Amen.
